# Joining a social club at Freed-Hardeman University can be a rewarding experience that offers numerous benefits. Here are some reasons why you should consider joining a social club:

    Community and Friendship: Social clubs provide an excellent opportunity to make new friends and connect with like-minded individuals. They often have a strong sense of community, and being part of such a group can make your college experience more enjoyable and fulfilling.
    Networking: Joining a social club allows you to expand your social network on campus. Networking with fellow club members can lead to valuable connections in various fields, both during your time at FHU and in the future.
    Leadership and Personal Growth: Many social clubs offer leadership positions and opportunities for personal development. Taking on leadership roles withinA group of smiling young adults, some holding books and backpacks, walk together outdoors in front of a building with glass doors. The atmosphere appears friendly and energetic. a club can help you develop valuable skills such as communication, teamwork, and organizational abilities.
    Campus Involvement: Being part of a social club means you’ll be more involved in campus life. These clubs often organize events, activities, and community service projects, allowing you to contribute positively to the university environment.
    Diverse Interests: Freed-Hardeman University likely offers a wide range of social clubs that cater to various interests, hobbies, and passions. Joining a club that aligns with your interests can enhance your college experience and make you feel more at home.
    Academic Support: Some social clubs may have academic-focused components, where members can study together, share resources, and support each other academically.
    Reduce Stress: College life can be stressful, and being part of a social club can provide a support system to help you cope with the challenges of university life.
    Resume Building: Involvement in social clubs can be a valuable addition to your resume. Employers often look for candidates who have demonstrated leadership, teamwork, and active participation in extracurricular activities.
    Memories and Traditions: Social clubs often have their own unique traditions, events, and memories that contribute to the overall college experience. These shared experiences can create lasting memories and bonds among members.
    Exploring New Interests: Joining a social club can expose you to new hobbies, activities, andA lively group of fans wearing yellow and black cheer enthusiastically in bleachers at a sports event, with some standing and clapping while others sit and watch. Signs reading LIONS are visible on the seats. interests that you might not have considered before. It’s an opportunity to broaden your horizons and try new things.

Ultimately, the decision to join a social club at Freed-Hardeman University will depend on your personal interests, goals, and preferences. Take the time to explore the various clubs on campus, attend their events, and talk to current members to find the one that best aligns with your passions and values. Remember that college is a time for personal growth and exploration, and social clubs can play a significant role in that journey.

# Chi Beta Chi (XBX, Chi Beta)
Chi Beta Chi is a social club that was established in 1989. Our mascot is the eagle, our letters are XBX, and our colors are purple and gold. Our mission statement is to provide opportunities for our members to become active socially, physically, mentally, and spiritually. Chi Beta has so many opportunities for our members to serve God and to serve others through mission trips to Wisconsin, the City of Children, and through various service projects around Henderson. We strive to be competitive in intramurals, Makin’ Music, Homecoming, and we seek to grow through retreats, meetings, and by being an encouragement to one another. The qualities we look for in our members are: Character, Leadership, Service, Tradition, and Royalty.

# Omega Chi (OK)
Omega Chi is the newest club on campus. Established in 2022, we are confined by nothing but strive to excel in everything. Our motto is “For the pursuit of excellence.” This club was created by students who do not fit the mold of existing stereotypes. Here, you are free to be exactly who you are but challenged to become what The Lord has designed for you to be. We don’t look for skill, style, or status, but good people who love to have a good time and serve their good God in all they do. Our mascot is the panther. Like the panther, we are unique and exist in a diverse environment in which we thrive. Years from now, the members will continue to grow and succeed because of the foundation that the members of today establish. The Omega Chi panthers are here to stay.

# Phi Kappa Alpha (PKA, Phi Kappa)
Established in 1938, Phi Kappa Alpha was created for men and women whose purpose was to exemplify and serve God in everything they do, to hold to the traditions of the past, and to strive to be a club of excellence on this campus. Phi Kappa Alpha will always compete to strive for the best in everything we do whether its Homecoming, Makin’ Music, or intramural athletics. Our motto is “Truth, Beauty, and Wisdom” which demonstrates the characteristics that transform the members of Phi Kappa Alpha into legends.

# Sigma Rho (Sig)
Sigma Rho is the oldest club on Freed-Hardeman’s campus and is founded on strong principles of family and tradition. We are characterized by our Greek letters, the Sigma standing for strength and the Rho for wisdom. We wear our black and gold colors with pride, the same way our Sigma Rho brothers and sisters wore them 101 years ago and the same way they will be worn 101 years from now. We bees have many mottos that are frequently used, but there is one that stands out among the rest. Our motto comes from a poem written by a club member many years ago. “It is the love I have for the things WE’VE done, that is why I am a Sigma Rho.” We don’t need a reminder that only the strong survive or anything like that because we don’t survive…we thrive. We thrive through the great memories we’ve made with one another. We thrive as we grow together in our spiritual walks with God. We thrive because we care about each other. We thrive because we are Sigma Rho.

# Xi Chi Delta (XC, Xi Chi, XCD)
Xi Chi Delta was established in 2002 by a group of friends who wanted to make a difference on Freed-Hardeman’s campus. It remains as FHU’s only social club started by students for students. Our colors are navy and silver and our mascot is a Knight. The slogan of Xi Chi Delta is K.N.I.G.H.T.S., “Keeping Nothing Inside Glorifying Him Through Service.” Our foundation remains fixated on God, the single Being Who unites all of our hearts together in perfect unity. We live for Him and He lives through us. Xi Chi Delta is not defined by anything. We do not fall under any category. We love God and we love each other.
